Promise Robotics raises C$40 million to expand its homebuilding factory network

The new Series B backs automated production services, with more than 2,500 housing units contracted rather than completed.

PR Newswire / Promise Robotics ↗17 November 2026English editorial summary
Story

New financing follows commercial agreements

Promise Robotics announced a C$40 million Series B on November 17, led by White Star Capital with Horizons Ventures, Radical Ventures and PSP Investments participating. This is a new financing development, distinct from the D.R. Horton commercial agreement covered in October. The amount is denominated in Canadian dollars.

Builders buy production capacity

Factory-as-a-Service translates existing home designs into robotic production plans for structural components and coordinates factory operations with installation. Builders can access capacity without developing and running their own factories. Manufacturing, transport and onsite assembly still need coordinated schedules for that capacity to support completed homes.

Operating sites and planned capacity

Production is live in Calgary and Nisku, with more than 2,500 housing units under contract across three markets. The first US facility, in Phoenix, is planned for 2027. Contracted units are not completed homes, and the total should not be added to the D.R. Horton commitment as if the figures described wholly separate pipelines.
